newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. recommends six-month renewal of Lebanon force. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.N. recommends six-month renewal of Lebanon force. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan recommended on Monday a six-month renewal, until July 31, of the U.N. peacekeeping force in southern Lebanon.

In a written report to the Security Council, he said while the "level of hostilities was somewhat lower than in the past, the situation in southern Lebanon continued to be tense and volatile, as Israel maintained its occupation of parts of the area, while Lebanese groups continued their attacks against the occupying force."

The 4,500-member U.N. Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) was established in 1978 to restore the Lebanese government's authority over the region after an Israeli incursion against Palestinian guerrillas (corrects).

After Israel withdrew its troops following a 1982 invasion, it set up a so-called security zone along the Lebanese side of the border, aided by its allies of the South Lebanon Army militia, to block attacks against northern Israel, now mainly by Iranian-backed guerrillas.
The U.N. chief said UNIFIL's original mandate, which called for a complete Israeli withdrawal, was unfulfilled.

Referring to an agreement reached after an Israeli offensive last April against guerrillas of the Islamic Hizbollah organisation, he said: "As regards firing into populated areas, the parties exercised a measure of restraint, in accordance with the understanding of April 26, 1996. It is hoped that they will continue to do so.

"However, this positive development should not obscure the fact that the inherent instability of the situation and the ever-present possibility of renewed deterioration remain a cause for serious concern."

Although UNIFIL continued to be prevented from implementing its mandate, "its contribution to stability and the protection it is able to afford the population of the area remain important," Annan said, recommending acceding to a Lebanese government request for another six-month extension.

He also drew attention to a serious shortfall in UNIFIL's funding resulting from unpaid assessments of $177 million, representing money owed to troop-contributing countries. He appealed to all U.N. members to pay their assessments.

UNIFIL, which costs $125 million a year, comprises contingents from Estonia, Fiji, Finland, France, Ghana, Ireland, Italy, Nepal, Norway and Poland. It is commanded by Maj. Gen. Stanislaw Wozniak of Poland.

The United Nations also called on the parties to find a solution to the case of a 65-year-old Palestinian accommodated at UNIFIL headquarters since April 1995 after being deported by Israel and denied entry by Lebanon.
